Rendered into each page's HTML at build time (src/story/pagehead.ts); the deck uses the story's markup, so {{stat}} tokens and [text](src:id) links resolve against the built data and sources.json. topCity, outcomes, claims and sources are counted from the data when the page is built.

deployments.title: Houston Has the Most Mapped Flock Cameras, and Texas Helped Pay for Thousands
deployments.deck: Volunteers have mapped {{topCity.flock}} Flock cameras inside Houston’s city limits, more than in any other U.S. city, though several smaller cities have more per resident. In Texas, at least $30 million from [a $1 fee on auto insurance policies](src:texastribune-abbott-2026) helped state and local agencies install at least 3,200 of the company’s cameras before the governor paused state funding on Aug. 27.

components.title: The 14 Parts Inside a Flock Camera
components.deck: The Falcon’s case is [8.75 inches long](src:flock-techspecs) and weighs about 3 pounds. It reads plates with its own processor and sends each read over a cellular connection; it has no network cable.

data.title: A Hot-List Match Reaches Officers in Seconds; Reads Are Kept for Days or Weeks
data.deck: When a plate matches a list, an alert reaches officers in [10 to 15 seconds](src:flock-flex-datasheet) on average, Flock says. The read is kept for [seven days](src:flock-guardrails-2026) by default for new customers; existing customers keep the periods they set, and Evidence Mode has no published limit.

journey.title: Tracking One Plate Read From a Flock Camera to Deletion
journey.deck: A car passes a Falcon camera. The photos and the plate it reads go to Flock’s cloud, are checked against hot lists and can be searched by the camera’s owner and the agencies it shares with, until they are deleted: after [seven days](src:flock-guardrails-2026) by default for new customers.

outcomes.title: Few Agencies Publish What Their Flock Cameras Produce
outcomes.deck: Of {{outcomes.sites}} places with a published result, {{outcomes.matched}} can be tied to a camera on the map within 150 meters. A handful of police departments publish audits of reads, alerts and arrests, and each counts them differently.

claims.title: {{claims.total}} Common Claims About Flock Cameras, Checked Against the Public Record
claims.deck: The record supports {{claims.true|ap}} of them and does not support {{claims.false|ap}}. On the other {{claims.nuanced|ap}}, the record is mixed: the answer depends on the product, its settings or which evidence is weighed.

economics.title: A Flock Camera Lists at $3,000 a Year, and Flock Keeps the Hardware
economics.deck: The [annual fee covers](src:flock-impl-guide) the camera, pole, solar panel, cellular data and software. Installation, permits, moves and replacements are billed separately.

sources.title: {{sources.total}} Sources, From Flock’s Own Documents to Court Records
sources.deck: Every document cited on this site: {{sources.flock}} from Flock Safety, {{sources.independent}} news reports, studies and reports by advocacy groups, and {{sources.public}} government and court records, with the date each was last checked.
